text:
alex: Hey infra — onboarding new customer account `redwood-helix` tomorrow. We need quota increases in eu-central-3 for p5, p4d and g5 families plus ENI limits. Can someone spin up the AWS request and link the case?

priya: I can take this. Quick verification: which exact instance counts do we want to request for initial ramp? Also need to know if they want On-Demand or Dedicated Capacity (Reserved) quotas.

alex: Start conservative but sufficient for early trials: p5.xlarge -> 8, p4d.24xlarge -> 2, g5.12xlarge -> 12. These are max concurrent instances. We'll request On-Demand + ability to convert to dedicated later. ENI attachments per AZ look low for this account — request bump to 300 ENIs.

sam: Putting rough cost calc: if all live at once monthly burn ~ $85k (on-demand). If they convert to reserved/dedicated it'd be cheaper. Flagging finance for approval if needed.

kai: FYI, eu-central-3 is a new region for us — we need to pre-warm limits for VPC, ENIs, and possibly EBS gp3 throughput. Also ensure the account has increased EC2 allocation for VCPU. I'll check existing service-quotas.

priya: Opening support case now. Short justification: "New production tenant for Redwood Dedicated requiring GPU capacity for inference validation and warm standby. Need predictable capacity during rollout window (2 weeks)."

infra-bot: Case opened: `CASE-2026-058742` — AWS replied asking for: region, account ID, instance family, desired quota, use-case, expected sustained hours/day.

alex: Reply to AWS with: account 987654321000, region eu-central-3, request ON-DEMAND quotas: P5 family -> 8, P4d family -> 2, G5 family -> 12, ENI per AZ -> 300, VCPU soft limit -> 700. Use-case: low-latency inference fleet for early customers with autoscaling and burst needs.

priya: Sent details to AWS. Pasted CLI for reference 
```
aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-F117E3F6 --desired-value 12 --region eu-central-3
```
(Replace quota-code per family; I included details in case case reply asks.)

sam: AWS asked for timeline and whether we plan to use spot. I replied: 2-week ramp, primary on-demand, spot for non-critical batch jobs. Also mentioned fallback to smaller quantized models to reduce instance count.

kai: I raised internal networking ticket to ensure subnets have free IPs and route tables are ready across AZs. Also cross-checked our ENI-per-instance mapping for GPU hosts — some AMIs attach extra ENIs for nvlink monitoring. That inflates attachments; calling it out in the case.

infra-bot: AWS responded: provisional approval for ENI increase pending verification. For GPUs they requested confirmation of software stack and instance lifecycle. Next step: share AMI IDs and expected startup scripts.

alex: Sharing AMI list and bootstrap script in thread — @kai, can you attach the AMI IDs here so AWS has them?

kai: AMIs added: ami-0b1a2c3d4e5f6a7b8 (gpu-runtime-v2), ami-0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d2 (monitoring-lite). Also noted startup attaches one extra ENI for monitoring: ~1.2 ENIs per host effective. I've told AWS to account for that.

priya: AWS case updated with AMIs and expected sustained hours (18/day). They set a tentative approval window of 48-72 hours. Case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=CASE-2026-058742

sam: Great. When approved, we need an action plan to validate capacity: 1) smoke boot 1 of each instance type 2) run perf sanity 3) ramp to 50% target 4) run cost check and handover to platform ops. I'll draft a runbook.

alex: Thanks team — please add any missing ask (IAM roles, KMS access, bucket policies) in the case before AWS finalizes. We want zero blockers when they enable quotas. :thumbsup:
